fields.meta_title: Employee Handbook Acknowledgment Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee handbook acknowledgment form that ties each signature to a handbook version and reminds anyone unsigned. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Handbook Acknowledgment Form by Version
fields.hero_description: Build an employee handbook acknowledgment form that records which version each employee signed, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Six Parts of an Acknowledgment You Can Prove
fields.features_subheading: The employee handbook acknowledgment form Emergent builds keeps the version and date behind every signature, refusals included.
fields.feature_1:
Each signature tied to one version

The app saves every e-signature with the handbook version number and the minute it was signed. A signature on version 4 stays with version 4 after version 5 goes out.
fields.feature_2:
A statement about receipt, not agreement

The app shows your statement above the signature line. Keep it to receipt: the employee got the handbook and can ask questions, not that they agree with each policy.
fields.feature_3:
A fresh round for each revision

Publishing a new handbook version asks every current employee to sign again. Start a round when a policy is added or changed, and skip it for a fixed typo or phone number.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders until the last person signs

The app emails a reminder to anyone still unsigned after the number of days you choose. When the deadline passes, HR gets a Slack alert with the names of everyone left.
fields.feature_5:
A recorded way to decline

Employees who will not sign can say so on the form and add their question. The app then asks their manager and a witness to sign a refusal note, filed with the record.
fields.feature_6:
Records you own, code you can export

Acknowledgments are stored in a database you own, and the form has no response cap. Paid plans from Standard up export the full code to a GitHub repository you control.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Moments a Signature Has to Hold Up
fields.tab_content_1:
Before his first shift, version 4 is signed

Brackwater Freight sends every new hire the acknowledgment link the day before they start. Mateo Ilarde reads handbook version 4 on his phone, types his name, and draws his signature. His record shows version 4, signed March 2 at 6:40 AM, before his first shift.
fields.tab_content_2:
After version 5, 41 of 48 signed in 3 days

Tessaly Dental Group published handbook version 5 with a new PTO policy and sent the acknowledgment to all 48 staff. Within 3 days, 41 of 48 had signed. Anyone unsigned after 3 days got an email reminder. The other 7 each found a link to version 5 in their inbox.
fields.tab_content_3:
Russ said no, so a manager and a witness signed

Russ Ambler won't sign handbook version 2 at Kestrel Lane Bakery until someone explains the overtime policy. He picks the option "I decline to sign for now" and types his question. Manager Bettina Ruel and witness Karl Ingersen sign the refusal note, which is filed with his record.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who signed version 3, when, and what he saw

Wren Toft needs to know what Peter Lamb signed before a dispute over shift swaps at Sable Ridge Veterinary. She opens his record: version 3, signed June 14 at 4:02 PM, the statement he saw above the line, and his signature. She sends the record to the practice owner.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Acknowledgment Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an employee handbook acknowledgment form that ties every signature to a version, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the statement as a receipt
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose the fields on the form
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give people a way to decline
fields.howto_step_1_des: Give the current handbook a version number and an effective date, and print both on its cover. In a dispute, HR needs to retrieve the exact handbook version, the acknowledgment language shown with it, who signed, and when. The number makes the first one easy.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write two or three sentences for the employee to sign: they received the handbook and know whom to ask about it. Clarify that the acknowledgment only confirms receipt of the handbook, not personal agreement with each item. Read it aloud once before you publish it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the printed name, the signature, and the date, and fill in the handbook version for the employee so nobody types it wrong. Add a space for a witness as well. You will want it ready on the day someone declines to sign.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put a second choice next to the signature: decline to sign for now, with a box for the question behind it. When someone picks it, have a manager and a witness sign a refusal note, and file the note with that employee's record.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the statement and the refusal rule into the prompt as you would brief a colleague. Emergent builds the form from that prompt, along with the database that keeps one record per signature. Later edits to the wording are another prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide how many days an employee has to sign, such as 3, and what follows: an email reminder to the employee, then a Slack alert to HR naming everyone still unsigned. Pick the hour the reminder goes out as well.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Sign it yourself, then decline it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign the form as one test employee and decline it as another. Open both records and confirm that the signed one carries the right handbook version, and that the refusal note is waiting for a manager and a witness.

faq_plan.q: What is a handbook acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a handbook acknowledgement form?

prov.original: What is a handbook acknowledgement form?

faq_plan.a: A handbook acknowledgment form is the page an employee signs to confirm they received the company handbook. A good employee handbook acknowledgment form names the handbook version, says the employee will read it and ask about anything unclear, and ends with spaces for the printed name, signature, and date.

faq_plan.q: How to create an acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.ref: How to create an acknowledgement form?

prov.original: How to create an acknowledgement form?

faq_plan.a: Decide what the employee confirms, write it as two or three plain sentences, and put a signature field under them. Describe that to Emergent's AI form builder, and it builds the form and a database with one record per signature. Each acknowledgment form built this way changes later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: Can you provide an example of an employee acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.ref: Can you provide an example of an employee acknowledgement form?

prov.original: Can you provide an example of an employee acknowledgement form?

faq_plan.a: Yes. A warehouse can send new hires one screen that reads: I received version 4 of the employee handbook, effective March 1, and I know to ask my supervisor or HR about anything unclear. Below it sits a signature line, with the version already filled in. Forms built on Emergent have no response caps, even in a month with 200 new hires.

faq_plan.q: What fields should an acknowledgment form template for new hires include?
faq_plan.a: Seven: the printed name, job title, start date, handbook version, the statement, the signature, and the date signed. Collect payroll details and emergency contacts on an employee information form instead. The acknowledgment then stays one screen long, and the signature sits right under the statement it covers.

faq_plan.q: When does a separate policy acknowledgment form make sense?
faq_plan.a: When one policy changes between handbook editions or needs its own signature, such as a new harassment policy or a phone rule on the warehouse floor. That policy acknowledgment form names the single policy and its effective date. The handbook form keeps covering the whole book, version by version.

faq_plan.q: What does an employee handbook acknowledgment form template say?
faq_plan.a: It should say the employee received the handbook, knows whom to ask about it, and understands it may change. A common clause has the employee agree that the handbook can undergo changes at any time, with or without notice. Have an employment lawyer word any at-will or contract language.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free acknowledgment form that collects e-signatures?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing, and the apps it builds can capture e-signatures. Describe the statement and the fields, and the employee list behind it can later feed an employee evaluation form when review season comes around.

faq_plan.q: How do I record a refusal to sign an employee acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.a: Give them a decline option on the form with a box for their question, then have the HR representative and a neutral witness sign the refusal note. Talk through the question first, since the form confirms receipt rather than agreement with each policy. Keep the note in the same record as the version they declined.

faq_plan.q: How often should employees sign a new handbook acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.a: After every change that matters. One HR guide says acknowledgment forms should also be sent out to existing employees as often as there are significant handbook updates or changes. On Emergent, every round's signatures stay in a database you own, beside the earlier versions.

faq_plan.q: Can employees without a work email sign an acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. They can open the link on their own phone or sign on a shared tablet at the front desk. If that tablet already runs a sign out form for equipment or visitors, add the acknowledgment as its own page. Have a supervisor check the unsigned list at the start of each shift.
